svg.aria-label: An illustrative hunt. From a ransomware report, a supervisor agent splits the hunt among narrow agents, each given only the tools and context its one job needs, because a local model does best with one job: forming a hypothesis, writing and running the detection logic, reporting. The Hypothesis agent's hunch is that attackers hide in scheduled tasks. The Detection agent's first search, for schtasks.exe, comes back empty, and empty does not mean safe: tasks made through the Task Scheduler API never launch schtasks.exe, so it rewrites the query, checks it and searches the event logs another way, around event 4698, a task being created. That returns 32 tasks created; one is unusual, \WinTaskUpdate, on one host and not in the baseline. The Reporting agent writes it up as a lead with the evidence attached, and only a human analyst makes the call.
